title: Kaomoji: Copy & Paste Cute Japanese Text Faces (◕‿◕)
meta_description: Copy and paste kaomoji with one click. Cute Japanese text faces for every mood: happy, sad, love, cat, sparkle and shrug ¯\_(ツ)_/¯. Also spelled kamoji.
hero_tagline: Copy and paste kaomoji: Japanese-style text emoticons built from Unicode characters. Happy faces, sad faces, shrugs, animals, and action expressions. Click any face to copy it instantly.
intro: Kaomoji (顔文字) are emoticons that originated in Japan, built from standard keyboard characters and Unicode symbols. Unlike emoji, kaomoji are read horizontally and often capture nuanced expressions that emoji can't fully convey. They paste into any text field that accepts Unicode text and add personality to messages, bios, and captions.

faq.a: A kamoji is a Japanese-style text emoticon: a little face built from standard keyboard and Unicode characters, like (◕‿◕), ¯\_(ツ)_/¯, or (｡•́︿•̀｡). Unlike emoji, kamoji are read upright rather than sideways, so the eyes, mouth, and arms are easy to recognise at a glance. Every kamoji on this page is plain text you can copy and paste into a bio, caption, or comment.

faq.q: Is kamoji the same as kaomoji?
faq.a: Yes. Kamoji is simply a common shortened spelling of kaomoji (顔文字), the Japanese term for text-based emoticons. The two words refer to exactly the same thing, text faces such as (^▽^) and (T_T), so searching for kamoji or kaomoji brings up the same kind of faces.

faq.q: How do I copy and paste a kamoji?
faq.a: Click any kamoji on this page to copy it instantly, then paste it into an Instagram or TikTok bio, a Discord or WhatsApp message, or a YouTube comment. Because each kamoji is pure Unicode text rather than an image, it pastes as text. Discord reads underscores as italics, so a face that contains them, such as the shrug, can arrive changed; wrapping the face in backticks keeps every character.

faq.q: What is the difference between a kamoji and an emoji?
faq.a: An emoji is a single coloured picture character rendered by the device's emoji font (😀), while a kamoji is a face assembled from ordinary text characters that you read upright, like (≧◡≦). Kamoji are more flexible and expressive for nuanced moods, and because they are built from standard Unicode text, no app swaps in its own picture.
